- Confirm whether Redwood will accept the standard EU SCCs (2021) with the usual tech/security exhibits attached, or propose an alternative.

Can your team turn around the redline review + evidence list by close of week? We’re aiming to execute the order by 12/03 to meet our pilot timeline.

Soojin / Ben — quick technical notes after skimming CloudHealth redlines:

1) Key management: CloudHealth requests customer-managed keys for certain workloads. We currently support KMS integration in Dedicated and Private modes; for Hosted API we use provider-managed KMS. We can offer envelope encryption and a dedicated KEK for this account under Dedicated capacity commitments.

2) Subprocessor routing: suggest adding language limiting cross-border subprocessors for EU-sourced data and adding a playbook to escalate exceptional routing.

3) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): recommend a short TIA that attaches to the DPA and:
   - lists transfer destinations and legal basis (SCCs)
   - states that Redwood will notify customers of material changes to subprocessor locations within 30 days
   - includes a limited mitigation plan for non-EU residency (e.g., additional contractual safeguards or temporary processing stop-gap)

I’ve drafted suggested TIA bullets in kms_clause_suggestion.txt and flagged the clause numbers I think need small edits.

Karthik
Senior Privacy Engineer
Redwood Inference

Emma / Soojin / Karthik — I reviewed CloudHealth_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx and Karthik’s notes. High level: we can accept the substance of the SCCs but need small contract-level protections preserved. Key items and proposed position:

- SCCs: Redwood will adopt the EU SCCs (2021) as the baseline. We will: (a) attach SCC Annex as exhibit, (b) populate processor/processor roles in the exhibit, and (c) ensure the technical and organisational measures exhibit aligns with our SOC2 controls.

- Transfer Addendum: propose a short, focused Transfer Addendum (attached: proposed_addendum_redlines.docx) that:
  * enumerates transfer destinations and clarifies fallback routing (region + tier),
  * limits any unilateral right for cross-border routing without Customer consent for high-risk data categories,
  * requires prior notice (30 days) for changes to subprocessor locations.

- KMS/Keys: For Hosted accounts we cannot provide customer-managed keys unless the customer purchases Dedicated capacity or Private. We can offer stronger encryption-at-rest language plus the option to move to Dedicated for CMK. Note this is a commercial ask and should be reflected in the order form (capacity line item).

- Evidence: we can share SOC2 Type II (redacted), subprocessor roster, and our KMS architecture diagram (non-prod sanitized). Production on-prem retention policy is only available for Private deployments.

Ask: Emma, confirm whether CloudHealth needs CMK for Hosted during pilot or if envelope encryption suffices. Also confirm whether CloudHealth will accept a limited TIA that is time-bounded to the order term.

I attached the proposed redline for the addendum. If CloudHealth is ok, we can prepare a clean DPA + exhibit to attach to the order form.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Ben / Soojin / Karthik — thanks for the quick review and the proposed addendum. A few follow-ups from our side:

- CMK: For the pilot we do not require CMK for Hosted, envelope encryption will work. We will need CMK for production if Redwood can provide it under Dedicated. Please note we’ll need a pricing line in the order form for Dedicated KMS support.

- TIA scope: CloudHealth is comfortable with a time-bounded TIA but would like an explicit clause that requires Redwood to engage in remediation and, if remediation fails, to stop processing EU personal data until an alternative is in place.

- Analytics subprocessor: we have a carveout request to allow a named analytics provider for de-identified metrics. We proposed a limited-scope carveout in the comments (see CloudHealth_comments.pdf).

We can do the legal sync Thu 11/26 09:30 PT — I’ll send a calendar invite in a separate email.

Regards,
Emma

Emma — thanks. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned ahead of the sync tomorrow: 

1) SCCs: Redwood accepts EU SCCs (2021) as baseline. Redwood will provide populated SCC Annex upon signature.

2) Transfer Addendum (TIA): Redwood proposes a short TIA (attached previously) that includes: list of transfer destinations, notification obligations (30 days), and a remediation path. We can add the stop-processing clause you requested where remediation fails — legal will keep that narrowly scoped to high-risk data categories.

3) CMK / KMS: For pilot envelope encryption is acceptable. We will add a dedicated order form line for CMK/Dedicated capacity if CloudHealth elects production CMK later.

4) Analytics subprocessor carveout: We are open to a named carveout for a de-identification analytics provider, subject to standard subprocessor vetting and contractual safeguards. We’ll flag this during the sync.

Request for you: please confirm the attendee list on the sync and any specific paragraph numbers you want to prioritize. We’ll come with a clean DPA + proposed TIA and an evidence pack for auditors.
